column1: # Names worked out by reading the decompiled function, with tools/re/batch.py for context.
# Only functions whose purpose is unambiguous from the body are named here; anything needing a guess is
# left as FUN_, because a wrong name in a database several people rely on costs more than a blank one.
# Script command arguments carry a 3-bit tag in their first word: bit 0 means "this is an instance
# property index rather than a literal", and bits 1-2 are the type - 0 int, 1 angle, 2 float. The three
# readers are GetScriptIntArg (0x209A68), GetScriptAngleArg (0x209AB0) and GetScriptFloatArg (0x209A00),
# and each tests (arg & 6) for its own value.

column1: # Cutscene mode lives in a 6-bit field of GameController + 0x8, bits 44-49. BeginCutsceneMode requires 0xC
# and moves to 0x34; EndCutsceneMode requires 0xD and moves to 0x2C; both also accept 0x7 as a lighter
# variant that only touches the letterbox. Bit 0 of GameController + 0x10 is "the letterbox is up".

column4: state 0xC to 0x34: takes control, raises the letterbox, clears the bottom text
state 0xD to 0x2C: lowers the letterbox and returns control
only in state 0xC: clears the text and raises the strip

column1: # SegmentTriangleDistances and ReadEdgeTestsFromVu0 are ONE routine that Ghidra sees as two functions.
# The first computes six edge tests into VU0 registers vf17, vf18, vf22, vf23, vf27 and vf28 and returns
# only the two plane distances through memory; the second reads those six registers back. They are coupled
# through coprocessor state, not through arguments or memory, so neither can be decompiled on its own and
# nothing may run between them. RayTriangleIntersect calls the second one from the middle of its condition

column4: signed distances of both segment endpoints from the triangle plane; leaves six edge tests live in VU0
drains vf17/18/22/23/27/28 - the six edge tests the call before it left behind
